newsitem.title: USA: Two 500 kv SoCal Edison power lines back.
newsitem.headline: Two 500 kv SoCal Edison power lines back.

text.p: Southern California Edison (SoCal Edison) said Wednesday two 500 kilovolt (kv) high-voltage transmission lines near Los Angeles resumed service after a light plane crashed into them Tuesday.

A 750 megawatt (MW) unit at the Ormond Beach power plant in Ventura County, which tripped off line due to a voltage dip caused by the line outage, also returned to operation, company spokesman Steve Conroy said.
"The lines and the (Ormond Beach) unit came back into service the same day," Conroy said.

Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC), the group overseeing the operation of the western states' power grid, estimated the system disturbance interrupted 18 percent of SoCal Edison's electric load.
WSCC said the disturbance also affected the system used by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.
The line and plant outage occurred when air-conditioning demand in southern California soared to record highs yesterday.

Conroy said sweltering heat of over 100 degrees Fahrenheit in inland areas around Los Angeles caused equipment failures, and that 2,500 customers in Ventura, Los Angeles and San Bernadino counties were still without power early Wednesday morning.
SoCal Edison, based in Rosemead, Calif., is a subsidiary of Edison International.
